issues.description: The board never uses the colours the extension contributes. VS Code 1.140 names webview colour variables "vscode-" + id.replace(".", "-"), which replaces only the first dot. So telelean.node.formalizedAura becomes --vscode-telelean-node.formalizedAura, but board.css reads --vscode-telelean-node-formalizedAura and --vscode-telelean-kind-*, which are never defined, so it always falls back to charts.*. I confirmed this in the real webview (probe P2-theme): with a colour customisation of #ff00ff for the aura, the aura still followed charts.blue, rgb(18, 52, 86). The colour contributions are therefore dead, and workbench.colorCustomizations for them are ignored, even though the CSS comment says they apply. Nobody notices with default colours, because the defaults equal the fallbacks. The Chrome harness never defines these variables, so no test catches it. M1 will add more contributed colours on the same pattern.
issues.suggested_fix: Use colour ids with a single dot (e.g. telelean.formalizedAura, telelean.assumptionKind, ...), or reference the escaped names: var(--vscode-telelean-node\.formalizedAura, var(--vscode-charts-blue)). Add a harness fixture that sets the contributed variable to a distinctive colour, with a Playwright assertion that the aura and glyph use it. Optionally have the 'rendered' diagnostic report the resolved aura colour, so the smoke test checks it in real VS Code.

issues.description: CSP violations caused by the HTML document itself are never reported. The listener is attached only when the module bundle runs, so a refused stylesheet (or a refused script) fires before it exists. In probe P1c (stylesheet blocked), smoke test 2, 'loads under the CSP ... renders the graph', still passed: an unstyled board with 4 cards and 3 arrows, column heights 144,18,36, and 0 csp-violation messages. Only test 3's 'stubs > 0' caught it. Separately, the builder's evidence that a grep of the logs for 'Refused to' found nothing is uninformative: in P1a, where the bundle was fully blocked, the logs contain no such line either.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach the securitypolicyviolation listener earlier, in a tiny nonce-tagged classic script loaded before the stylesheet link that buffers violations in a global, and let the bundle forward them. Add a style check to 'rendered' (e.g. getComputedStyle(.tl-col__list).overflowY === 'auto' and equal column heights) and assert it in test 2.

issues.description: The validator accepts a kindChange where from === to (a no-op kind change) and a theseSuffice with duplicate premises (['a','a']). A diagnostic data key named __proto__ is silently dropped. All harmless while the host only logs, but in M1 the host will act on these messages.
issues.suggested_fix: Reject kindChange when from === to, and reject or de-duplicate repeated premises. Optionally reject reserved keys in data instead of dropping them.

issues.description: Visual polish, seen both in the Chrome screenshots and in the real VS Code capture (verify-board/p2-spyro-crop.png): when Derivations is empty, the A→G arrows run straight through the 'No derivations yet' text. The '▲/▼ n linked' badges also cover text on the first and last visible cards and take their clicks (the builder already disclosed this; it is worse at the real webview's 846 px width).
issues.suggested_fix: Move the empty-state text out of the arrows' path, or give it a background. Draw the badges in a header/footer strip of each column instead of over the cards.

issues.description: Chrome cannot start with TMPDIR set to the scratchpad path: 'FATAL:process_singleton_posix.cc:313] Socket path too long: .../verify-board/tmp/com.google.Chrome.OcDDxQ/SingletonSocket'. Playwright runs therefore fall back to /tmp, where Chrome can leave empty /tmp/com.google.Chrome.chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_.* directories. Seven of these are timestamped 06:58–07:13, which matches the builder's Playwright runs; the builder's report does not mention them. One appeared in my first run and I removed it.
issues.suggested_fix: Give Chrome a short per-run temp dir (launchOptions.env.TMPDIR) and remove it afterwards, or add a cleanup step. Disclose it in the run notes.

notes:
**Verdict.** All the spike's main claims survived my attempts to refute them. "needs-work" is driven by one cheap major fix (the theme variable names) and some test-gap polish; nothing invalidates the spike.

**Confirmed independently:**
- **Inside real VS Code 1.140.0:**
  - The bundle runs under an enforced nonce CSP with no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' (P1a, P1b).
  - Violations raised after the bundle starts are detected and fail the smoke test (P1b).
  - The three columns scroll independently, and the arrows and stubs follow every scroll, checked with my own geometry code (P2).
  - Geometry is cached: no getBoundingClientRect calls while only scrolling.
- **In Chrome:** drag-and-drop between columns, multi-select with the tray, the A|D|G box, the chevron, the aura, high contrast, the badge click and reorder within a column all work.
- **Fidelity:** core types and samples match 03 sections 2 and 3.3 (Lean snippets, and block ranges checked against test-fixtures/spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean). The protocol is {v:1,type,payload}, with every host-bound message validated. The command, CSP, localResourceRoots, CJS bundle with vscode external, and output channel are as specified.
- **Tests:** the builder's tests are meaningful. The arrow checker compares real card boxes, and its non-vacuity test works.

**Observations, not defects:**
1. The 'rendered' message arrives before the frame is painted. An xwd dump taken the moment it arrived still showed the empty "Waiting for the extension…" board; the next dump (150 ms later) was the full board, identical to one at 750 ms. 'Settled' signals for M2 should not assume paint.
2. 'rendered' decides it has settled by comparing card counts. Two graphs in a row with the same node count could therefore be reported from the previous DOM; tagging the engine stats with the applied version would be safer.
3. Stubs are short hooks on the visible card plus a badge at the hidden column's edge. That is a reasonable reading of "stub at the column edge" and of D-13.

**Method and files** (all under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn2/verify-board/):
